source: The processor that executes instructions — often called the 'brain' of the computer.
Volatile working memory the CPU reads/writes directly; its contents are lost when power is off.
Storage built from flash memory chips instead of spinning platters, so it's faster with no moving parts.
Combines multiple physical disks into one logical unit for redundancy, performance, or both.
Translates human-readable domain names (like example.com) into IP addresses.
The protocol web browsers use to request and receive pages from a server.
Creates an encrypted tunnel over a public network so traffic behaves as if it's on a private one.
Automatically assigns IP addresses and network settings to devices as they join a network.
